caption:
AI coding platform OpenCode says attackers got into a legacy system and may have exposed OpenAI, Anthropic and Google API keys saved by about 1.4% of its Console users.
It calls it a large scale distillation attack. Some users reported fast draining balances.
If you linked provider keys to OpenCode Console, revoke and replace them now.

Do you store your AI API keys in third party tools?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Cybersecurity News

slides.headline: Hackers just got into OpenCode and may have your *OpenAI and Claude keys*

slides.heading: A *forgotten system* got hit
paras: OpenCode, an open source AI coding platform, says someone gained unauthorized access to a legacy system it was in the process of shutting down.
It emailed affected users on Saturday, October 17. Users who did not get an email were not affected, the company says.

slides.heading: *Your keys*, their bill
paras: About 1.4% of Console users who linked outside AI providers are in scope. Their stored OpenAI, Anthropic and Google API keys may have been exposed.
OpenCode calls it a large scale distillation attack, meaning someone harvests answers from top models to train their own. Some users reported balances draining fast.

slides.heading: One user lost *$1,700*
paras: Developer Preston Zeller reported losses of $1,700, Dealroom says. OpenCode has not said how many keys were taken or whether it will refund victims.

paras.t: If you linked keys to OpenCode Console: revoke and replace them in each provider's dashboard, update your apps and check recent usage.

slides.hook: One leaked key can drain your AI budget overnight. Follow for the security news that protects your wallet.
